title: Batch 13 verify leftovers (doc drift, missing tests)
description:
- [JMAP-wf92.5] minor crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs: Missing negative test for the alias removal (fc81085f). The old test backend_changes_error_limit_zero_maps_to_cannot_calculate was deleted and nothing replaced it. CHANGELOG says 'A zero limit now maps to tooManyChanges like any other value', but no test checks it: no 'limit: 0' appears anywhere in crate-jmap-server src or tests. Only limit 50 is tested. Suggested fix: add a test that TooManyChanges { limit: 0 } produces error_type TooManyChanges with limit Some(0), not cannotCalculateChanges.
- [JMAP-wf92.5] minor crate-jmap-chat-client/src/methods/message.rs: Doc drift: the module doc at line 12 still says message_create inspects `error_type == "rateLimit"`. The code at line 314 now compares against jmap_types::SetErrorType::RateLimit, so the doc should name the typed variant.
- [JMAP-wf92.5] minor crate-jmap-server/src/response.rs: New wire behaviour without a test: RequestError now also sends description as RFC 7807 'detail' on a limit error (CHANGELOG: 'now also sends a description as detail'). request_error_limit_includes_limit_property only checks 'limit' and 'type'. No test builds a limit error with a description and asserts both 'limit' (from limit_name) and 'detail' (from description). The testjig ws.rs send_request_error path changed the same way and is also untested.
- [JMAP-dpbp] minor crate-jmap-chat-server/src/message.rs: store_server_message(backend, caller, account_id, chat_id, sender_msg_id, build) now takes the dedup keys separately from the builder. Its rustdoc says the built Message's chatId/senderMsgId MUST equal chat_id/sender_msg_id, but nothing checks it (no debug_assert or error). The old API took one prebuilt Message, so the keys and the stored values could not disagree. Every in-tree caller complies, so this is not blocking. A cheap fix is a post-build equality check that returns an error (or debug_assert) when stored.chat_id != *chat_id or stored.sender_msg_id != *sender_msg_id.
- [JMAP-wf92.3] minor AGENTS.md: Line 93 (crate table entry for crate-jmap-peer-auth) still says SignedRequest::parse/verify does "checks 1-6, caller-supplied clock, keys and replay lookup". After this change, verify runs checks 2, 3, 4 and 6, takes no replay lookup, and leaves check 5 to the caller's atomic test-and-insert. The fix commit removed the same wording from the README and lib.rs but missed this file. (The "replay lookup" at CHANGELOG.md:970 is in an earlier release's entry and is fine.)
- [JMAP-wf92.3] minor crate-jmap-peer-auth/README.md: Lines 12-13 now read "You pass in the clock, the peer domain's fetched `peerSigningKeys`, your DNSSEC validation result." Removing the last list item also removed the "and", so the sentence is a list with no conjunction. It should read "... `peerSigningKeys` and your DNSSEC validation result."
- [JMAP-ace5] minor crate-jmap-vtc-server/src/call.rs: update_call passes from = [call.state] from the handler's earlier read (L579). If the call moves pending/ringing -> active before the write, a moderator's VTCCall/set state:"ended" is refused with invalidProperties, even though active -> ended is a listed transition. end_cascade (L937-381) has also already ended and CAS-stopped the breakout rooms and their recordings by then, so the parent stays active while its rooms are ended. This is a partial side effect, and the window is narrow (end_call checks `from` before the cascade, but update_call does not re-check it). Spec conformance is not broken (no MUST is violated, and the transition into 'ended' is never wrong), but re-deriving the reason from the refused state, as end_cascade already does for rooms, or checking the parent's CAS before the cascade, would remove both effects.
- [JMAP-ace5] minor crate-jmap-vtc-server/tests/state_race.rs: decline_end_of_an_answered_call_is_refused calls end_call(&[Ringing], Declined) directly. Nothing tests the participant.rs call_transitions wiring, where a VTCParticipant/set decline reads a ringing call that has meanwhile become active, through the Racing backend. A regression that drops `&[CallState::Ringing]` at participant.rs:1096 would go unnoticed.
- [JMAP-wf92.4] minor crate-jmap-base-client/src/client.rs: extract_response now decodes the error object strictly with JmapError's Deserialize. Any malformed modeled property, not only a missing `type`, turns the whole MethodError into ClientError::Parse, and the server's error type is lost. Examples: `limit` as a string or a negative number, or an `existingId` that fails Id validation. That matches the RFC-typed fields (UnsignedInt, Id). But the docs in error.rs, client.rs and the README and the CHANGELOG name only 'no type' as the Parse case. Consider saying 'missing or malformed type/description/existingId/limit'. Not blocking.
- [JMAP-wf92.6] minor crate-jmap-tasks-client/README.md: Doc drift: method table lines 72 and 77 still document `task_query(filter, sort, position, limit)` and `task_notification_query(filter, sort, position, limit)`; signature is now `(filter, sort, &QueryParams)`.
- [JMAP-wf92.6] minor crate-jmap-vtc-client/README.md: Doc drift: line 73 table row still says `<T>_query(filter, sort, position, limit)` although this README was edited in the commit (example updated) and the methods now take `&QueryParams`.
- [JMAP-wf92.6] minor crate-jmap-filenode-client/README.md: Doc drift: line 81 lists `file_node_query` params as `filter, sort, position, limit, depth`; now `filter, sort, &QueryParams, depth`.
- [JMAP-ip5u] minor crate-jmap-filenode-client/README.md: README examples (L37-59) call `file_node_set` with 4 args; the method is `filenode_set` and now takes 5 (create, update, destroy, if_in_state, params), so the second example passes Some(params) in the if_in_state slot. The method name and the FileNodeSetParams literal (missing `extra`) were already wrong before this range; the sweep added the argument-count drift and did not update this README, unlike the contacts/tasks/vtc/sharing READMEs.
- [JMAP-wf92.11] minor CHANGELOG.md: The CHANGELOG entry ('Every `/query` comparator `property` is a typed enum...') and the AGENTS.md exception ('Every comparator's `property` is a typed enum ... never a plain `String`') overclaim. These QueryObjects still use `type Comparator = serde_json::Value`: Calendar, CalendarEventNotification, ParticipantIdentity (calendars-types/src/backend.rs), Mailbox and EmailSubmission (mail-types), Principal and ShareNotification (sharing-types), TaskList (tasks-types) and FileNode (filenode-types). The bead's own scope only names the String-typed and closed-enum comparators, so this is not a coverage gap in the code. The two documents should either say 'every typed comparator' or name these untyped ones as out of scope, possibly with a follow-up bead.
- [JMAP-wf92.11] minor crate-jmap-vtc-server/tests/call_query.rs: Missing server-level negative tests. Before this change, an unlisted sort name failed the typed decode, so `unsupportedSort` was automatic. Now each server depends on its `KnownSort` impl. Server tests send an unlisted property for VTCCall, the four Scene types, the five Chat types, Graph, GraphNode and GraphNodeOp. Nothing does the same for VTCParticipant/query, VTCRecording/query, VTCLivestream/query or GraphEdge/query. The `known_sort!` impls do cover those comparators (vtc-server/src/helpers.rs, graph-server/src/helpers.rs), and the types-level tests only show that the name decodes to `Other`, not that the server rejects it.
- [JMAP-wf92.12] minor crate-jmap-chat-client/src/ws.rs: The ChatPresenceEvent malformed-body fallback (line 53, `.ok()` then `Other(frame)`) has no negative test. Only the ChatTypingEvent malformed path is tested (parse_chat_typing_malformed_keeps_raw). This gap existed before the commit, but the commit now promises raw-JSON preservation for both event types. A test like the typing one, with a presence frame missing required fields, would cover it.
- [JMAP-wf92.12] minor crate-jmap-chat-client/src/ws.rs: No test checks that WsFrame::Response is passed through as Other(WsFrame::Response). StateChange, Unknown and RequestError passthrough are all tested. This was also untested before the commit. The `let-else` makes it structurally obvious, so this is low risk.
- [JMAP-wf92.8] minor crate-jmap-chat-filenode-server/tests/rights.rs: The bead exists to make the @everyone floor per Space, but no test checks it per Space. Every test backend (MemoryBackend, Fed, Bound) returns the same set for every Space, so if the code passed the wrong Space to everyone_permissions (for example the channel's Space instead of call.spaceId in vtc, or a different Space in filenode or federation), every test would still pass. Fix: add a test backend that keys its answer on space.id, seed two Spaces with different floors, and assert that the checked Space's floor decides the result. Not blocking: reading the code at all 5 call sites (vtc lib.rs:116, filenode member_permissions, deliver.rs:658) shows the correct Space is passed.
- [JMAP-wf92.8] minor crate-jmap-chat-federation-server/src/deliver.rs: The new error paths have no tests. These are: Peer/deliver step 5 returning serverFail when everyone_permissions fails (named in the CHANGELOG), RootCheckError::Chat from the filenode bindings, and the C::Error from check_call_create. FaultyBackend in crate-jmap-chat-server/tests/common/mod.rs returns Err, but no test of a binding or of the federation handler uses it.
- [JMAP-wf92.9] minor crate-jmap-calendars-types/src/availability.rs: Doc drift: the BusyPeriod type-level doc still cites draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 §2.2, while the new BusyStatus enum, the field doc and the updated tests cite -33 §2.2. The line was already there before this range, but the commit touched this struct and updated the other citations.
- [JMAP-wf92.13] minor crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/lib.rs: Line 159 cites `crate-jmap-mail-server/src/lib.rs:133-148` for the 'Re-registration semantics' section; this commit moved mail lib.rs up by about 5 lines (URI consts and backend re-export block removed), so the section header is now near line 129 and the range lands mid-section. Doc drift caused by this commit; cite the section by name or fix the range.
- [JMAP-wf92.13] minor crate-jmap-mail-types/src/lib.rs: Outside bead scope, for the record: the calendars, chat, contacts, filenode, mail, sharing and tasks types crates still have `pub mod backend` together with root `pub use backend::{...}`, so their property enums have two public paths. The bead covers server crates only (contacts-types only for `collision`); not blocking.
- [JMAP-wf92.16] minor crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/lib.rs: Doc drift: line 257 still says the MockBackend field `copy_called` records whether `copy_contact_card` was called. That method was replaced by `copy_object` in 514c31a1.
- [JMAP-wf92.16] minor crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/memory.rs: Doc drift: lines 143-145 say `apply_contact_card_index_delta` is called from `copy_contact_card`. That method is now `copy_object`, which calls the delta only when `O::TYPE_NAME == "ContactCard"`.
- [JMAP-wf92.14] minor RELEASING.md: The reqwest 0.13 explanation overstates the case. It says `rustls-no-provider` panics in `ClientBuilder::build` unless a process-wide CryptoProvider is installed, and that 0.13 has no ring-backed TLS without global setup. In reqwest-0.13.5 src/async_impl/client.rs, the panic only happens in `default_rustls_crypto_provider` (line 2499), which runs when no preconfigured TLS is given. `ClientBuilder::use_preconfigured_tls(rustls::ClientConfig)` (line 2239, which takes the `TlsBackend::BuiltRustls` branch at line 644) lets you build a ring + webpki-roots client per client, with no global install. The decision to stay on 0.12 still holds, because clients passed in by callers cannot be forced onto that path. But the text should mention `use_preconfigured_tls` and say the real obstacle is caller-built clients, not that it is impossible.
- [JMAP-wf92.17] minor crate-jmap-mail-server/README.md: Bead item 6 (w1lm) is not fully covered. The commit updates the supports_type summary in the calendars, chat, contacts (README and PLAN), filenode (README and PLAN), sharing and tasks docs, but crate-jmap-mail-server/README.md L141 still reads 'Return true if this account supports the given JMAP object type.' crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs L463 already uses the canonical 'Returns `true` if this backend supports JMAP object type `O` for `account_id`, as seen by `caller`.' The wording here starts with 'Return' rather than 'Returns', which is probably why a grep for the old text missed it. This is doc drift only; behaviour is unaffected.
- [JMAP-wf92.15] minor crate-jmap-calendars-types/AGENTS.md: Doc drift: the commit updated the client and server AGENTS.md but not this one. Lines 9, 33, 42, 65, 101 and 124 still call draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 normative, say 'Field names must match draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 exactly', and point to a -26 reference path (jmap-chat-spec/references/, which does not exist). That conflicts with the -33 names this commit adds (participant, iCalendar, Id sort) and would steer later agents back to -26 names. Smaller instances of the same drift: the test doc comments in crate-jmap-calendars-types/tests/filter_strictness.rs (lines 32, 41, 51) still cite -26 (the cited sections still exist in -33).
- [JMAP-wf92.15] minor crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/event.rs: Missing test: CalendarEvent/copy now fills an omitted @type/version through prepare_new_event (line 854), and the commit message and CHANGELOG both say so, but only the set-create path has a test (lib.rs set_create_fills_omitted_type_and_version). No test copies a source event that lacks version.
close_reason: D batch: committed, adversarially verified, CI green at f8dfe002
